correctness.rationale: The reversal-invariant P4 adjacency and complement split into explicit 2x2 blocks with traced eigenvalues plus/minus sqrt5/2. Matrix exponentials yield every pairwise amplitude and the complex f contrast. The same-class min/max and opposite-class trigonometric optimization provide global upper bounds, including balanced equality 2/(1+sqrt5). Irrationality of sqrt5 makes the joint phase trajectory dense on a 2-torus, establishing each claimed sharp supremum over all real times. The packaged independent Taylor-matrix verifier checks 12864 scalar equality comparisons and 116733 phase-grid bound pairs; finite checks are not substituted for the density theorem. No normalization, absolute-value or exceptional-pair gaps remain.

value.rationale: P4 is the smallest connected nonregular self-complementary simple graph. The complete pairwise four-observable sharp values serve as a canonical physically motivated benchmark for paired quantum transport, giving nontrivial cross-degree amplitudes 2sqrt(2/5) and 2/5 below individual-transfer ceilings. This directly quantifies simultaneous transport obstructions hidden by single-walk bounds; it is a natural complete small-system classification rather than an arbitrary graph entry. It does not promise device performance or larger-path transfer theorems.
